findings.documented: API key should be appended as a query parameter: ?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: Passing api_key as a query parameter returns HTTP 401: 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'. API key must be sent in header 'X-API-Key'.
findings.how_found: Tested initial GET /v1/listings query parameter call before writing application code.
findings.impact: All frontend and client requests fail with 401 if key is passed via URL query parameter.

findings.documented: Returns object with 'token', 'expires_in': 86400 (24h), user name, and specifies no refresh flow exists.
findings.actual: Returns 'access_token', 'refresh_token', 'refresh_url': '/auth/refresh', 'expires_in': 900 (15 minutes), and user object without 'name' field.
findings.how_found: Inspected POST /auth/login payload response upon successful authentication.
findings.impact: Sessions expire in 15 minutes instead of 24 hours unless refresh tokens are utilized via /auth/refresh.

findings.documented: Login response returns user object with 'name': 'Demo User'.
findings.actual: Login response user object returns only {'email': '...'}, omitting 'name' completely.
findings.how_found: Inspected response body of POST /auth/login.
findings.impact: Frontend code accessing user.name receives undefined unless a fallback or email-derived display name is used.

findings.documented: POST /auth/logout invalidates the current token server side.
findings.actual: POST /auth/logout returns {'ok': true, 'note': 'tokens are stateless; discard them client side'}. The server maintains no token blacklist and tokens remain valid until expiration.
findings.how_found: Sent POST /auth/logout and reused bearer token on subsequent GET /v1/listings request.
findings.impact: Client-side logout must explicitly clear cached tokens from localStorage and memory as server-side invalidation is a no-op.

findings.documented: Collection endpoints require only your city-scoped API key.
findings.actual: Endpoints return 401 'missing bearer token - log in at POST /auth/login first' if Authorization Bearer header is missing.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings with X-API-Key header but without Authorization header.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated users cannot browse listings or projects without first logging into a user session.

findings.documented: Pagination uses 1-indexed 'page' and 'limit' (default 20, max 200). Response shape contains total, page, page_size, results.
findings.actual: Pagination uses 0-indexed 'offset' and caps 'limit' at 50 (requesting limit=500 returns limit=50). Response shape contains limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings?limit=500&page=2 and inspected total envelope properties.
findings.impact: Page-based client pagination logic breaks; offset-based pagination must be implemented with limit 50 max.

findings.documented: Response total field reports the exact number of matching records retrievable.
findings.actual: Response envelope reports total: 4907 for listings, but paging offset to completion yields 4950 retrievable records (43 more than reported). Similarly rentals report total 2020 but yield 2050, and projects report 568 but yield 590.
findings.how_found: Fetched all pages to completion until has_more was false and counted total returned objects.
findings.impact: Progress bars and page calculations based on envelope 'total' terminate prematurely before reading all dataset records.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: Endpoint returns 1,058 inactive/archived listings with is_live: false. Inactive listings are not excluded server side.
findings.how_found: Inspected is_live boolean across all 4,950 returned records (3,892 live vs 1,058 inactive).
findings.impact: Clients that do not filter by is_live will show sold, expired, or withdrawn properties to end users.

findings.documented: Listing and rental schemas document fields without an 'is_live' property.
findings.actual: Both listing and rental records contain an undocumented 'is_live' boolean flag denoting listing active status.
findings.how_found: Examined object keys on returned listing and rental records.
findings.impact: Developers unaware of is_live cannot distinguish between active and inactive properties.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregate statistics for your city.
findings.actual: Endpoint returns HTTP 404 {'detail': 'Not Found'}.
findings.how_found: Sent GET request to /v1/analytics/summary with valid headers and auth token.
findings.impact: Insights screen cannot fetch server-side pre-computed summaries and must compute aggregates client-side.

findings.documented: GET, POST, and DELETE /v1/favourites endpoints allow logged-in users to persist saved property listings.
findings.actual: All /v1/favourites endpoints return HTTP 404 {'detail': 'Not Found'}.
findings.how_found: Tested GET and POST requests to /v1/favourites with valid user session bearer token.
findings.impact: Favourites cannot be stored on the remote backend and must be managed via client-side localStorage per user.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} (singular) returns a single property listing.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns HTTP 404 {'detail': 'Not Found'}. The actual working route is plural: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}.
findings.how_found: Sent request to GET /v1/listing/100-5000042 and compared with GET /v1/listings/100-5000042.
findings.impact: Following the documented singular path results in 404 errors on all single property detail lookups.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings in the same locality.
findings.actual: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns HTTP 404 {'detail': 'Not Found'} for all listing IDs.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar across multiple listing IDs.
findings.impact: Property detail pages cannot fetch server-side similar listings strip and must calculate fallback recommendations client-side.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings?project_id=P... filters listings belonging to a specific builder project.
findings.actual: Query parameter project_id is quietly ignored by the server, returning all city listings regardless of project ID.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings?project_id=P50001 and inspected project_id fields in the returned items.
findings.impact: Frontend project detail views must perform client-side filtering on listing records by project_id.

findings.documented: GET /v1/rentals filters rental listings by specified criteria.
findings.actual: Query parameters 'property_type', 'min_price', and 'max_price' are silently ignored on /v1/rentals, returning all 2020 rental listings without filtering.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/rentals?property_type=villa and /v1/rentals?min_price=100000 and observed unchanged envelope total of 2020 with apartments and cheap rentals returned.
findings.impact: Client applications must implement client-side filtering for rental property types and price ranges.

findings.documented: sort_by=carpet_area sorts listings numerically by carpet area in square feet.
findings.actual: sort_by=carpet_area sorts values lexicographically as strings (e.g. area 340 square feet appears before 32 square feet when order=asc).
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings?sort_by=carpet_area&order=asc and compared consecutive carpet_area values.
findings.impact: Server-side carpet area sorting returns incorrectly ordered results; client-side numeric sort is necessary.

findings.documented: GET /v1/rentals supports sort_by and Question 5 asks for monthly rent.
findings.actual: Calling GET /v1/rentals?sort_by=rent fails with HTTP 400 {'detail': "cannot sort by 'rent'"}. The field is named 'price'.
findings.how_found: Attempted to sort rentals by sort_by=rent.
findings.impact: Developers attempting to sort by the natural entity name 'rent' encounter 400 Bad Request errors.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max fields in builder projects represent price in Indian Rupees (INR) as integers.
findings.actual: price_min and price_max in /v1/projects are floating-point numbers representing prices in Crores of INR (e.g., price_max 12.44 represents 12.44 Crores = 124,400,000 INR).
findings.how_found: Compared project price_max (12.44) with actual listing prices (46,110,000 INR) for project P50016.
findings.impact: Unconverted project prices show as single/double digit numbers (e.g. Rs 12 instead of Rs 12.44 Cr) unless multiplied by 10,000,000.

findings.documented: total_listings in GET /v1/projects is recomputed whenever a listing is added/withdrawn and always agrees with listings count.
findings.actual: For 443 out of 590 projects, total_listings reported in GET /v1/projects differs from the actual count of listings in /v1/listings.
findings.how_found: Grouped all listings by project_id and compared counts with total_listings in project records.
findings.impact: Project cards display inaccurate listing availability counts unless computed directly from listing records.

findings.documented: Timestamps are formatted as ISO 8601 strings in UTC with an explicit 'Z' suffix.
findings.actual: All posted_at timestamps returned across listings, rentals, and projects are naive ISO 8601 strings without 'Z' or timezone offsets.
findings.how_found: Inspected raw posted_at string values across all fetched records.
findings.impact: Date parsers without explicit UTC handling may parse timestamps in local browser timezone causing timezone offset errors.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: 19 duplicate clusters (38 total listing records) describe identical physical properties (same locality, apartment, floor, bedrooms, carpet area) listed across different agencies.
findings.how_found: Grouped listings by physical property specifications (locality, apartment_name, floor, total_floors, bedrooms, carpet_area).
findings.impact: Property listings page shows duplicate physical apartments under different listing IDs and slightly varying prices.

findings.documented: Listing records describe valid physical properties; inactive or corrupt listings are excluded server-side.
findings.actual: 41 listing records contain physical impossibilities (floor > total_floors, carpet > super built-up area, negative prices, swapped latitude/longitude coordinates).
findings.how_found: Ran automated physical constraint validation checks on all 4950 retrievable listing records.
findings.impact: Unvalidated listing data causes UI rendering bugs (e.g. floor 18 of 10, negative listing prices, map markers in the ocean).

findings.documented: is_verified means our operations team has checked the listing.
findings.actual: Multiple listings with physically impossible and corrupt data (such as negative prices ranging from -1.4 Cr to -6.4 Cr) have is_verified: true, showing the verification flag is unvalidated.
findings.how_found: Cross-referenced corrupt negative-price listings against the is_verified attribute.
findings.impact: Users relying on is_verified as a trust signal are exposed to blatant data corruptions.

findings.documented: posted_by_contact is the seller's verified contact number.
findings.actual: All 856 unique seller phone numbers across listings use the fictitious unallocated prefix '+91200...', which are not real or verified Indian mobile numbers.
findings.how_found: Validated phone number formats against Indian telecom E.164 allocation standards.
findings.impact: Clicking or calling seller contact numbers fails to connect to actual home sellers.

findings.documented: /v1/listings contains genuine property sale listings.
findings.actual: 11 listing records are bait/fake listings where monthly rental amounts (Rs 17,470 - Rs 44,440 total price) are listed as sale property prices to generate enquiries.
findings.how_found: Calculated price per square foot across all sale listings and identified extreme price anomalies (< Rs 500/sqft in Mumbai).
findings.impact: Users sorting by price ascending encounter fake bait listings priced at monthly rental values.
